# Jubilees Chapter 36 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Isaac's testament; the division of the land between Jacob and Esau

---

**36:1** In the first year of the seventh week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Isaac called his sons Esau and Jacob to him, and they came.

**36:2** He said to them: "My sons, I am going the way of all the earth. Today I divide my inheritance between the two of you and give each of you a portion.

**36:3** Arise and hear what I say, so that you may do it and not die before your time.

**36:4** Honor your mother, for she is the mother of you both. And love one another, my sons; do not despise one another in your hearts.

**36:5** Love your brother; let no hostility arise between you. Do not be like brothers who are enemies to each other.

**36:6** Do not let the spirit of Mastema have dominion over you or your descendants, and do not let him bring you into destruction and condemnation.

**36:7** For I know that Esau will be jealous and angry toward you, Jacob, because of the blessing I have given you. But I command him to do you no harm."

**36:8** He called Esau and said to him: "I am an old man and I am about to die. My eyes are dim and my strength has failed.

**36:9** You have seen what I gave to your brother Jacob, and you see that he has received more than you. Yet I have given you much as well, and I have apportioned an inheritance to both of you.

**36:10** Go to the mountains of Seir and rule over them. Your domain extends from the east to all the boundaries of Edom. Jacob will rule over Canaan and all the land from the river to the sea.

**36:11** Do not transgress against your brother Jacob and do not take any of his inheritance from him. Love him with all your heart and with all your soul, and let there be peace between you both.

**36:12** If he serves you faithfully and with a good heart, do not count it as a burden, for he is your brother. If he serves you faithfully, it is good. But if you are found to be treacherous, I will curse you at my death."

**36:13** Esau said: "I will do all that you have commanded me. I will not transgress against my brother Jacob. He is my brother."

**36:14** Isaac was pleased by Esau's words and blessed him: "May the LORD God of Israel bless you and prosper your way, and may he multiply your descendants, and may your descendants possess all that your heart desires."

**36:15** Isaac blessed Jacob and said: "Jacob, my son whom I love — may God bless you from above, from the dew of heaven and from the richness of the earth.

**36:16** May God Almighty bless you and prosper your way, and may your descendants be many and multiply greatly."

**36:17** Isaac called his two sons again and gave them his testament. He divided the whole land of Canaan into portions for Jacob and gave the mountains of Seir to Esau.

**36:18** He said: "I have given the whole land of Canaan to Jacob and to his descendants after him forever. To Esau I have given the mountains of Seir and all that is in them."

**36:19** After many days, Isaac died. Jacob and Esau buried him at Mamre in the cave of Machpelah, beside their grandfather Abraham.

**36:20** Jacob and Esau wept greatly for Isaac, and all their household wept with them.

---

*LOGOS notes: Isaac's deathbed testament is a formal legal document in Jubilees, assigning Canaan to Jacob and Seir to Esau. The Mastema warning (v.6) is one of only a few direct mentions of Mastema in the patriarchal section. The geographical division here clarifies what Jubilees sees as the divinely ordained boundary between Israel and Edom.*
